summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on model catalog: selecting open models, reading benchmark numbers, and how the compatibility matrix drives deployability across hosted, dedicated, and private modes. Customer wants predictable latency for inference at 8-12 token/s per request, strong data residency and KMS integration, and low-cost options for high-throughput batch jobs.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. I'm Olivia from Redwood, AE on the account. with me are Marco, our SE, and Priya from Product. quick intro from Verdant?
[00:10] Emily Shaw: Hi all, Emily here, CTO at Verdant. we're building an NLP layer for clinical triage and scheduling, so latency and PHI controls are big.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: Ravi, Head of ML, we'll be owning the model side and POC.
[00:22] Laura Kim: Laura, eng manager, I'll coordinate infra.
[00:25] Samir Khan: Samir from security, will look at SOC2 and KMS.
[00:30] Olivia Chen: Awesome. Today we'll demo the model catalog in the Console, look at benchmarks, and walk thru the compatibility matrix — basically how you pick an open model and understand whether it fits hosted, dedicated, or private deployment. we'll leave time for questions and next steps.
[00:45] Marco Diaz: (screen shares) ok jumping into the console — top left is the model catalog, you can filter by task: chat/generation, embeddings, reranking. here we've curated open models and also show Redwood-verified profiles — each entry has throughput and latency p50/p95 numbers, token-cost estimates, and recommended quantization.
[01:10] Ravi Patel: sorry quick Q — those latency numbers, are they for hosted infra or dedicated?
[01:15] Marco Diaz: good question — we show both. the default card shows a profile for our hosted cluster (multi-tenant) at typical seq len 128, plus a link to dedicated benchmarks for different GPU families (A100, H100, L4). the compatibility matrix (right column) maps model variants to hardware + quantization options.
[01:35] Laura Kim: the compatibility table — is that automated or manually curated?
[01:40] Priya Rao: it's a mix. we run an onboarding suite that measures kernel compatibility, memory footprint, kv cache behavior; then we annotate recommended quantization (e4, int8-fp8 etc) and note known regressions. some of the entries have human notes for edge cases.
[01:58] Emily Shaw: do you have examples for 4k context and long inputs? our use has transcripts often 2-3k tokens.
[02:05] Marco Diaz: yes, for long-context we show separate profiles; the card will list a longer-seq latency sample, and we have guidance on chunking + prefix KV cache. one caveat — some open models degrade in perf when quantized aggressively for longer seqs, we call that out in the matrix.
[02:25] Ravi Patel: another practical question: cost estimates per token — are those just infra cost or include Redwood margins?
[02:30] Olivia Chen: the cards show a unit estimate which is infra-backed (GPU-hour normalized) and then our pricing overlays. the benchmark sheet we send will have raw perf numbers + modeled cost scenarios you can plug your QPS into.
[02:42] Marco Diaz: jumping to a concrete example — here's an Llama-2-13B variant, compatibility shows it's supported on A100 with int8 quant, recommended for latency-sensitive generation up to seq 512. p50 70ms per 64 tokens on dedicated A100; on hosted multi-tenant it's about 90ms.
[03:02] Ravi Patel: hmm those p95 numbers matter for SLA. what's your observed p95 under bursty traffic?
[03:08] Marco Diaz: depends on batching config. we provide batching policies — you can set max latency SLO and Redwood Optimize will suggest batching windows and cache policies. p95 on dedicated with conservative batching around 200ms SLO tends to be within 2x p50. for hosted, it's wider during noisy neighbors, which is why we recommend Dedicated for strict SLOs.
[03:30] Samir Khan: on the private side, we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs — does the model catalog or console expose what variants are allowed under private deployment?
[03:40] Priya Rao: in the compatibility matrix we tag entries "private-ready" when kernels and licensing are compatible; there are also distro notes if a model requires certain OSS libs. for KMS, we have integrations documented and can support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated in VPC setup.
[03:58] Emily Shaw: licensing — any restrictions on model weights we should be aware of?
[04:03] Marco Diaz: we flag license types on each model card and have a license compatibility checker; for some permissive open weights it's straightforward, others require attribution or have non-commercial clauses — we'll surface that and can help legal review.
[04:20] Laura Kim: infrastructure question — for the POC we have on-prem GPUs (8x A10G). will the compatibility matrix advise on that hardware?
[04:30] Marco Diaz: yes, matrix rows include GPU families; for A10G we typically recommend different quant profiles — sometimes you get better throughput with bfloat16 than int8 on older cards. we'll include perf extrapolations but recommend running a tiny benchmark which we can help automate.
[04:48] Ravi Patel: can Redwood Optimize auto-suggest quantization profiles per workload? that would save us time.
[04:53] Priya Rao: Optimize provides profile suggestions based on your eval set and desired quality threshold. you run a short eval (we provide harness) against a few models and Optimize will rank models by cost/quality and recommend quantization and batching.
[05:10] Emily Shaw: how invasive is the SDK integration? our current stack uses Python microservices and a Rust ingestion pipeline.
[05:17] Olivia Chen: we have SDKs for Python, Go, Node, and a simple HTTP REST endpoint. for Rust you'll call the REST API or use community SDKs; the calls are standard: create-completion/chat, stream support, function-calls. Marco can share code snippets.
[05:33] Marco Diaz: (shares snippet) here is a sample curl and python snippet showing streaming; we also show how to pass model pins and rollout policies during the call.
[05:42] Laura Kim: about model pinning — can we pin to an exact model+quantized variant? we want stable results.
[05:48] Marco Diaz: yes, pinning is supported at model-version+profile level; you can lock the quantization profile and rollout to canary 5% then ramp. the Console exposes rollout controls and tracing hooks.
[06:05] Samir Khan: security question again — where are audit logs stored and how long? we need 13 months retention for some clients.
[06:13] Priya Rao: by default we retain logs 90 days but enterprise add-ons allow custom retention. audit logs for Private deployments can be forwarded to customer SIEM; dedicated customers can opt into extended retention. we'll include this in the SOC2 pack.
[06:30] Ravi Patel: any gotchas around KV cache when running multi-tenant hosted? we rely on prefix-caching to save cost.
[06:36] Marco Diaz: hosted supports prefix caching but it's ephemeral across tenants; for stronger guarantees we advise Dedicated where KV cache is managed per-customer. note that some models with large key-values will need increased memory and can affect packing efficiency. compat matrix flags that.
[06:54] Emily Shaw: per our SLA needs we'd probably look at Dedicated for production and maybe Hosted for dev. wanted to confirm if Redwood offers reserved capacity for bursts?
[07:02] Olivia Chen: yes, Dedicated has reserved pools and burst options; you can configure autoscale policies and reserve burstable spare capacity for peak windows. pricing-wise we do monthly commits.
[07:15] Laura Kim: can you walk through an example selection flow — like we have a goal: 100 qps, avg payload 80 tokens, p95 latency <500ms, budget target $X per month — how do we pick model and deployment?
[07:25] Marco Diaz: sure. first filter catalog by task and license. then sort by cost/latency. run a modeled cost calc: take p50/p95 and throughput numbers, apply your qps and seq len, factor quantization for token reduction. Optimize will then rank top candidates by cost/quality — often the recommendation is a smaller model on Dedicated with int8 for high qps use-cases.
[07:48] Ravi Patel: do you expose raw benchmark logs? I want to see the run output, traces, memory, kernel logs.
[07:53] Marco Diaz: yes, for POC we can share raw benchmark artifacts and a spreadsheet with the run metadata. we'll also give the test harness so you can rerun locally.
[08:05] Olivia Chen: ok quick pause — any other questions specific to Verdant's clinical data handling?
[08:12] Samir Khan: we need data residency in region us-west-2 and key control via AWS KMS, also encryption at rest and in transit, and SOC2 compliance evidence.
[08:21] Priya Rao: those are supported — for Private we can deploy control plane in your VPC or do a hybrid. we'll attach the SOC2 docs and the VPC checklist.
[08:32] Laura Kim: timeline: we want a POC with 2 models tested (one smaller, one larger) and initial benchmarks in two weeks, is that doable?
[08:38] Olivia Chen: yes, that aligns with our standard POC. Marco will drive infra setup and Priya will pick model candidates.
[08:45] Marco Diaz: action items: I'll share a POC runbook and sample infra templates. we'll need a short access window to your test VPC or you can run the harness and send logs.
[08:58] Ravi Patel: what's the typical time to get dedicated capacity? we've seen multi-week waits with other vendors.
[09:05] Olivia Chen: for Dedicated we have standard SLAs depending on commit and region; small pilot capacity often provisioned within 3-10 business days, larger reserved pools take longer. we'll coordinate with platform ops.
[09:20] Emily Shaw: ok sounds good.
[09:22] Olivia Chen: great — recap of next steps: I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and model compatibility matrix link, Marco will send the POC runbook and code snippets, Priya will share the security/SOC2 pack and compatibility notes, and we'll tentatively schedule kick-off for 2026-07-28. any final questions?
[09:40] Laura Kim: none from me.
[09:42] Ravi Patel: no, thanks.
[09:44] Samir Khan: thanks everyone.
[09:46] Olivia Chen: thanks all, will follow up by email with artifacts. bye.
